semantics.what: Prerelease version numbers consumed WITHOUT publication. A number is burned when its immutable v* tag exists at a commit that can never be released, so the number can neither be published nor reused. Read by scripts/release-audit-tags.mjs (npm run release:audit-tags), which lets successor chains step over declared burns; an UNDECLARED skip still fails the audit.
semantics.rules: Prerelease numbers only — a stable number must never be burned. Each entry requires a non-empty reason. An entry whose version the registry HAS published is itself a violation: publication consumes a number, burning does not apply.
semantics.how_to_burn: Add an entry here in the same PR that retargets packages/cli to the next number, with a reason naming why the tagged commit is unreleasable.

burned.reason: tag v0.1.0-pre.4 points at 9c81aecf, which predates the artifact-digest canonicalization fix (PR #238); the staged workflow runs the scripts as of the tagged commit, the v* ruleset makes the tag immovable, and the version was never published or staged

tag v0.1.0-pre.5 points at 12a59833, which predates the dry-run sentinel fix in receiptEmissionCommands; the tag is immovable, its dry run can never complete, and Brian chose a fully green dry rehearsal before first live use over taking pre.5 live on a diagnosed-but-unrehearsed path; never published or staged

tag v0.1.0-pre.6 points at 94a01342, whose release-staged.yml resolves the draft via the tag-addressed endpoint that cannot see drafts; workflow_dispatch runs the workflow at the dispatched ref and live mode requires a v* tag ref, so the tag can never pick up the id-based fix; its first live run created draft 368277129 and uploaded assets but crashed at capture; never staged or published

tag v0.1.0-pre.7 points at 1e2e2aa3, whose release-staged.yml passes the tarball to npm stage publish as a bare two-segment path that npm parses as github:owner/repo shorthand (live run 31499362043 died on git ls-remote before touching the registry); the immovable tag cannot pick up the ./-prefix fix; its draft (id 368610973) exists with assets; never staged or published
